comparison: Perfect agreement on transcriptomics data (C25-C28). Both evaluations find the expression patterns well-supported. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of the BrainSpan ATLAS analysis, while peer review implicitly accepts these findings without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on electrophysiology data showing functional differences (C29-C34). Both find the desensitization and agonist sensitivity data convincing. Peer review describes work as 'very rigorous and meticulous,' while OpenEval notes appropriate statistical analyses and experimental design. Peer review also includes summary claims C6 and C83.

Strong agreement on Neto modulation data (C40-C54). Both evaluations support the differential effects of Neto1 vs Neto2. OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of patch-clamp data, while peer review confirms the insertion 'changes the modulatory effects of Neto proteins.' Peer review also includes C7, C91-C92 regarding Neto effects.

Agreement on mutational analysis data (C55-C59), though OpenEval notes uncertainty about K368-E rectification mechanism (C59). Both accept the experimental rigor. Peer review groups this with co-IP and additional mutational claims (C8, C60-C67, C88-C90, C103) that OpenEval evaluates separately.

Agreement on co-IP and functional effects of mutations (C60-C67). OpenEval finds these claims supported by the data showing maintained protein interactions and differential functional effects. Peer review acknowledges the pull-down assays and mutagenesis work as part of mechanistic investigation.

Significant disagreement on structural data quality and utility (C68-C75). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with caveats about splice region resolution, while peer review rates UNCERTAIN, calling this 'the biggest weakness' due to low resolution (5-8 Å range) limiting mechanistic insight. Both acknowledge no major conformational changes observed.

Agreement on structural limitations (C95-C96). Both acknowledge poor resolution of the splice region. OpenEval views honest reporting of limitations as appropriate, while peer review emphasizes this prevents mechanistic conclusions and states 'more data are needed.'

Agreement on summary claims (C6-C8, C83). OpenEval finds these well-supported by comprehensive functional data. Peer review explicitly confirms these findings in editor's summary and reviewer comments, describing the work as convincing.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic interpretation about glutamate vs kainate pathways (C84-C85) as SUPPORTED with caveats. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific interpretive claims.

Partial overlap on K368-E mutant effects (C88-C90). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while noting speculative aspects of protein interaction mechanisms. Peer review acknowledges mutagenesis work broadly but doesn't specifically evaluate these mechanistic interpretations.

Partial overlap on Neto modulation mechanisms (C91-C94). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to speculative mechanistic interpretations about allosteric vs direct interactions. Peer review accepts differential Neto effects (C91-C92) but doesn't specifically evaluate the mechanistic proposals in C93-C94.

Implicit agreement on mechanistic uncertainty (C97-C101). OpenEval explicitly rates these structural mechanism proposals as UNCERTAIN due to poor splice region resolution. Peer review's criticism of structural data quality aligns with this assessment, emphasizing insufficient mechanistic insight.

OpenEval evaluates mechanistic hypotheses about differential Neto modulation (C86-C87) as UNCERTAIN, noting they are speculative. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found for these hypothetical mechanisms.

OpenEval finds summary and forward-looking statements (C102-C105) SUPPORTED as appropriate conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these summary claims, though peer review confirms overall importance of findings.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1-C2, C10-C18) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review does not evaluate these background claims as they are established literature context.

OpenEval finds knowledge gap statements (C3-C5, C19-C24) SUPPORTED as accurate motivation for the study. Peer review does not specifically evaluate these framing claims but implicitly accepts them by describing the work as 'important.'

OpenEval rates mechanistic proposal about rectification (C35-C37) as UNCERTAIN, noting C37 is speculative about allosteric mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific mechanistic interpretations.
OpenEval evaluates background claims about Neto proteins (C38-C39) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer review does not evaluate these background literature claims.

OpenEval finds context about alternative splicing and novelty claim (C76-C82) SUPPORTED. Peer review implicitly accepts novelty by stating findings 'advance our understanding' but doesn't specifically evaluate these contextual claims.
